nerd.ety:
Unknown. Attested since 1951 as US student slang.
* Perhaps an alteration of nerts (“nuts", "crazy”); see references below.
* The word, capitalized, appeared in 1950 in Dr. Seuss’s If I Ran the Zoo as the name of an imaginary animal:
*: And then, just to show them, I’ll sail to Katroo / And bring back an It-Kutch, a Preep and a Proo, / A Nerkle, a Nerd and a Seersucker too!
* Possibly a rebracketing of inert as a nert, as in he's inert = he's a nerd, in reference to one's lack of competence or athletic ability.
* Various unlikely folk etymologies and less likely backronymic speculations also e

ex.ja: オオカミは獲物が豊富な地域に住んでいる。

ex.ja: 彼女はかわいがっていた犬が事故で死んだ時、たくさんの涙を流した。

An act or process of degradation.

Food sold at a delicatessen.

To coat or decorate with enamel.
To variegate with colours, as if with enamel.

The ordinal form of the number fourteen.

en: In terms of geography.
To laugh gently in a playful, nervous, or affected manner.
A high-pitched, silly laugh.
Fun; an amusing episode.

en: A female host.
A female innkeeper.

hostess.ety: From Middle English hostesse, from Middle French hostesse, from Old French ostesce, made up of oste (“host”) + -esce (“feminine marker”).

ex.en: The hostess couldn't possibly put up with his arrogance.

ex.en: Let's drink to our charming hostess!

Of a thing, characterized by genius; cleverly contrived or done.

ex.ja: 離陸する時に、耳がキーンとなります。

ex.en: Please fasten your seat belt during takeoff and landing.
ex.ja: 離着陸の際にはシートベルトをしめて下さい。

note.ja: take off（離陸する）の名詞化。「離陸」。

en: That can be taxed.
Subject to taxation.
Something on which tax must be paid.
A piece of indoor sporting equipment used to allow for the motions of running or walking while staying in one place.
A mill worked by persons treading upon steps on the periphery of a wide wheel having a horizontal axis. It was used principally as a mean…
To exercise on a treadmill.
To keep busy, for example, with work or with other tasks, without being able to get ahead or make progress towards long-term goals.

treadmill.ety: From tread + mill. Its figurative senses refer to the idea that running on a treadmill requires continued effort and motion to remain in the same place.

ex.en: I broke a sweat running on the treadmill.
ex.ja: 私はトレッドミル上を走って汗をかいた。

note.ja: tread（踏む）+ mill（水車・粉ひき）。昔の囚人の踏み車 →「ルームランナー」→ 単調な繰り返しの仕事。

en: Impossible to avoid; bound to happen.
Not voidable; incapable of being made null or void.
Something that cannot be avoided.

unavoidable.ety: From Middle English unavoidable, equivalent to un- + avoidable.

ex.en: A sacrifice is unavoidable.
ex.ja: 犠牲はつきものさ。

ex.en: He had to part from her owing to unavoidable circumstances many years ago.
ex.ja: 彼は何年も前にやむを得ない事情のため、彼女と別れなければなりませんでした。

ex.en: Due to unavoidable circumstances this summer I can't stay in my holiday cottage.
ex.ja: よんどころない事情で、今年の夏は別荘で過ごせないんだ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ avoid（避ける）+ -able。「避けられない」。

en: Done by one side only.
Affecting only one side of the body.

unilateral.ety: A modern creation (circa 1802), from New Latin ūnilaterālis (“one-sided”), from Latin ūnus (“one”) + laterālis (“sided, lateral”), equivalent to uni- + lateral.

note.ja: uni（1つの）+ lateral（側の）。「一方の側だけの」→「一方的な」。bilateral（二国間の）と対。

en: To fight for superiority; to contend; to compete eagerly so as to gain something.
To do or produce in emulation, competition, or rivalry; to put in competition; to bandy.

vie.ety: Apheretic form of envy, from Middle English envien, from Old French envier, from Latin invītō.

ex.en: City firms vied with each other to hire the brightest young staff.
ex.ja: 都会の会社は有能な若者を採用しようと互いに張り合った。

note.ja: envy（ねたむ）の古い形 envien から。「競う」。

en: Any of many types of stinging flying insect resembling a hornet.
Any of the members of suborder Apocrita, excepting the ants (family Formicidae) and bees (clade Anthophila).
To move like a wasp; to buzz.

wasp.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *wóbʰseh₂
Proto-Germanic *wapsō
Proto-West Germanic *wapsu
Old English wæps
Middle English wasp
English wasp
Inherited from Middle English wappes, waps, wasp, waspe, from Old English wæfs, wæps, wæsp, from Proto-West Germanic *wapsu, from Proto-Germanic *wapsō (“wasp”), from Proto-Indo-European *wóbʰseh₂ (“wasp”), from *webʰ- (“to braid, weave”), referring to the insect's woven nests.
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian wesp (“wasp”), Saterland Frisian Häspe (“wasp”), West Frisian waps (“wasp”), Alemannic German Wespi (“wasp”), Bava

ex.en: Wasps and hornets are flying about.
ex.ja: 蜂が飛び回る。

ex.en: I got a nasty sting from a wasp.
ex.ja: スズメバチにこっぴどく刺された。

ex.en: "Have you ever been stung by a wasp?" "Yes – once, as a child."
ex.ja: 「スズメバチに刺されたことある？」「はい。子供の頃、一度だけ」

note.ja: 古英語 wæsp から。weave と同系で、巣を織る虫とされる。「スズメバチ」。

en: A plant of the species Citrullus lanatus, bearing a melon-like fruit.
The fruit of the watermelon plant, having a green rind and watery flesh that is typically bright red when ripe and contains black seeds.

watermelon.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *wed-
Proto-Indo-European *-r̥
Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥
Proto-Germanic *watōr
Proto-West Germanic *watar
Old English wæter
Middle English water
English water
English melon
English watermelon
Endocentric compound of water + melon. Compare French melon d'eau, German Wassermelone, and Spanish melón de agua.
The meanings referring to environmentalists and behind-schedule projects derive from the idea of having a green (eco-friendly, on-schedule) outward appearance while being red (socialist, behind schedule) in a hidden way comparable to that of the fruit.

ex.en: I've never seen such a giant watermelon!
ex.ja: こんな大きなスイカは見たことがない。

ex.en: In summer it's watermelon or nothing!
ex.ja: 夏はスイカに限る！

ex.en: In summer limit yourself to watermelon!
ex.ja: 夏はスイカに限る！

note.ja: water（水）+ melon（メロン）。「スイカ」。

en: Lying toward the west.
Moving or oriented toward the west.
Toward the west.
The western region or countries; the west.

westward.ety: From Middle English westward, from Old English westweard.

ex.en: The sun declined westward.
ex.ja: 太陽が西に傾いた。

en: To become wide or wider.
To make wide or wider.

ex.en: Television helps us widen our knowledge.
ex.ja: テレビのおかげで我々は知識を広めることができる。

ex.en: As time passes, your perspective widens.
ex.ja: 歳を重ねると見えてくるものがある。

ex.en: This road was widened last year.
ex.ja: この道路は昨年拡張された。

note.ja: wide（広い）+ -en。「広げる」。

en: A principle in Chinese and related East Asian philosophies associated with dark, cool, female, etc. elements of the natural world.
The number one, primarily used in Scotland and Ulster

yin.ety: From early romanizations of Chinese 陰／阴 (yīn), originally used in reference to shaded areas, as of a mountain or home.

note.ja: 中国語「陰」から。yang（陽）と対。

en: Of or relating to acid; having the character of an acid.
Having a pH less than 7, or being sour, or having the strength to neutralize alkalis, or turning a litmus paper red.

ex.en: The ocean is becoming more acidic.
ex.ja: 海は酸性になっていっている。

ex.en: When the ocean absorbs a lot of CO₂, the water becomes more acidic.
ex.ja: 多量の二酸化炭素を吸収すると海はより酸性になる。

ex.en: Lemons and limes are acidic fruits.
ex.ja: レモンやライムはすっぱい果物である。

note.ja: acid（酸）+ -ic。ラテン語 acidus（酸っぱい）。「酸性の」。acute と同系。

en: A close physical union of two objects.
Faithful support for some cause.

adherence.ety:

note.ja: adhere（くっつく・守る）+ -ence。ad + haerere。「遵守」。adhesive と同じ。

en: A word that modifies a noun or noun phrase or describes a noun’s referent.
Adjectival; pertaining to or functioning as an adjective.
Applying to methods of enforcement and rules of procedure.
To make an adjective of; to form or convert into an adjective.
To characterize with an adjective; to describe by using an adjective.

adjective.ety: From Middle English adjectif, adjective, from Old French adjectif, from Latin adiectivus, from adiciō + -īvus, from ad- (“to, towards, at”) + iaciō (“throw”). The Latin word adiectivus in turn was a calque of Ancient Greek ἐπιθετικόν (epithetikón, “added”), a derivative of the compound verb ἐπιτίθημι (epitíthēmi), from which also comes epithet.

ex.en: "Small" and "tiny" are adjectives.
ex.ja: 「小さい」と「ちっちゃい」は形容詞です。

ex.en: "Small" and "little" are adjectives.
ex.ja: 「小さい」と「ちっちゃい」は形容詞です。

ex.en: The next sentence has adjectives and adverbs.
ex.ja: 次の文には形容詞と副詞が含まれています。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ ject（投げる）+ ive。名詞に投げ添える語 →「形容詞」。

en: Loss of memory; forgetfulness.
Forgetfulness.

amnesia.ety: From modified Latin amnesia, from Ancient Greek ἀμνησία (amnēsía, “forgetfulness”), a noun derivation from μιμνήσκω (mimnḗskō, “to remind, to remember”) prefixed with the alpha privative.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 a（否定）+ mnēsis（記憶）。「記憶がないこと」→「記憶喪失」。amnesty と同じ。

en: Having been made the subject of amplification; more potent or stronger, louder

ex.en: They amplified their argument by new facts.
ex.ja: 彼らは新事実によって議論を発展させた。

en: In an angry manner; under the influence of anger.

angrily.ety: From Middle English angrily, equivalent to angry + -ly.

ex.en: "That's the one problem," he said angrily.
ex.ja: 「それが唯一の欠点だ」と彼は怒って言った。

ex.en: "That's the only problem," he said angrily.
ex.ja: 「それが唯一の欠点だ」と彼は怒って言った。

ex.en: "Leave me alone," she said angrily.
ex.ja: 「私の事は放っておいてよ」と彼女は怒って言った。

zh: 受理上訴的 /受理上诉的

en: That can be (legally) appealed to, especially of a court that hears appeals of decisions by a lower court.

note.ja: ラテン語 appellare（訴える）から。appeal と同じ。appellate court（控訴裁判所）。

en: The act of ascending; an ascent.
A transcendence of the material world; a transition to a higher form, state, or plane of existence.

ascension.ety: From Middle English ascencioun, from Old French ascension, from Latin ascēnsiō, ascēnsiōnem (“ascent”). Displaced native Old English upfæreld.

note.ja: ascend（昇る）+ -sion。ad + scandere（登る）。descend と同じ scend。

en: an analgesic drug, acetylsalicylic acid
A tablet containing this substance.

aspirin.ety: Genericized trademark of German Aspirin, from acetylierte Spirsäure (literally “acetylated spiraeic acid”). The trade name Aspirin is a registered trademark in some countries, but has entered the English language in generic usage, as various German trademarks were nullified in the United States after World War I (see also heroin).

ex.en: Do you by any chance have some aspirin?
ex.ja: ひょっとしてアスピリン持ってない？

ex.en: I would like to buy some aspirin.
ex.ja: アスピリンが欲しいのですが。

ex.en: Do you happen to have some aspirin?
ex.ja: ひょっとしてアスピリン持ってない？

note.ja: ドイツの商標名 Aspirin から。a（アセチル）+ Spiraea（シモツケ属の植物）+ -in。

en: A professional poet and singer, like among the ancient Celts, whose occupation was to compose and sing verses in honor of the heroic achi…
A poet.
To cover a horse in defensive armor.
To cover (meat or game) with a thin slice of fat bacon.

bard.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH-
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH-dʰh₁o-der.
Proto-Celtic *bardosder.
Old Irish bard
Scottish Gaelic bàrdder.
English bard
First use appears c. 1449. From Scottish Gaelic bàrd, from Old Irish bard, from Proto-Celtic *bardos (“bard, poet”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“praise”), and reinforced by Latin bardus, borrowed from Celtic. Cognate with Latin grātus (“grateful, pleasant, delightful”), Sanskrit गृणाति (gṛṇāti, “calls, praises”), Old Church Slavonic жрьти (žrĭti, “to sacrifice”).

note.ja: ケルト語 bardos（詩人）から。シェイクスピアは the Bard と呼ばれる。

en: Having a disposition to do good.
Possessing or manifesting love for mankind.

benevolent.ety: From Old French benevolent, borrowed from Latin benevolēns ("benevolent"). Displaced native Old English welwillende (literally well-wishing).

note.ja: ラテン語 bene（よく）+ volens（望む）。「よかれと願う」→「慈悲深い」。benefit、volunteer と同じ。

en: A book or other product that has sold in large numbers.

ex.en: It is said that the book is a bestseller in Britain.
ex.ja: その本はイギリスでベスト・セラーだそうだ。

ex.en: Manga are to the Japanese film industry what bestsellers are to Hollywood.
ex.ja: 漫画と日本の映画産業の関係は、ベストセラーとハリウッドの関係に似ている。

ex.en: Is it possible to acquire the bestseller in the bookstore in Akita?
ex.ja: そのベストセラーを秋田の書店で入手できますか。

note.ja: best（最も）+ seller（売れるもの）。「ベストセラー」。

zh: 布雷澤外套 /布雷泽外套

en: A very bright or hot day.
A dish used to cook directly over the coals of a brazier, or the flame of a chafing dish lamp.

blazer.ety: From blaze (“to reflect or send forth a bright light; (figurative) to be conspicuous; etc.”, verb) + -er (suffix forming agent nouns). Blaze is derived from blaze (“fire”, noun), from Middle English blase (“a flame, blaze; a firebrand, torch; a bright light”), from Old English blæse, blase (“a flame, blaze; a firebrand, torch”) (whence Old English blæsere, blasere (“one who burns, burner, incendiary”, literally “blazer”)), from Proto-West Germanic *blasā (“a flame, blaze; a firebrand, torch”), from Proto-Germanic *blasǭ (“a torch”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to blaze, burn; to be brigh

ex.en: I would like to get a blouse to go with this blazer.
ex.ja: このブレザーにあうブラウスがほしいのですが。

note.ja: blaze（燃え立つ）+ -er。ケンブリッジ大学のボート部の真っ赤な上着から。

en: An area of decayed vegetation (particularly sphagnum moss) which forms a wet spongy ground too soft for walking.
An acidic, chiefly rain-fed (ombrotrophic), peat-forming wetland. (Contrast an alkaline fen, and swamps and marshes.)
To sink or submerge someone or something into bogland.
To prevent or slow someone or something from making progress.

bog.ety:
Inherited from Middle English bog (originally chiefly in Ireland and Scotland), from Irish and Scottish Gaelic bogach (“soft, boggy ground”), from Old Irish bog (“soft”), from Proto-Celtic *buggos (“soft, tender”) + Old Irish -ach, from Proto-Celtic *-ākos.
The frequent use to form compounds regarding the animals and plants in such areas mimics Irish compositions such as bog-luachair (“bulrush, bogrush”).
Its use for toilets is now often derived from the resemblance of latrines and outhouse cesspools to bogholes, but the noun sense appears to be a clipped form of boghouse (“outhouse, privy”),

ex.en: We were bogged down in a morass of paperwork.
ex.ja: 私たちは書類事務の泥沼に陥っていた。

ex.en: Grounding and other bog-standard punishments didn't get through to his son at all.
ex.ja: 外出禁止とか、その他のありふれた罰を与えても、彼の息子には全く通じなかった。

note.ja: スコットランド・ゲール語 bogach（沼）から。bog（柔らかい）。「沼地」→ 沼にはまるように「行き詰まる（bog down）」。

en: The act of bombing, especially towns or cities.
Heavy artillery fire.

From bombard + -ment.

note.ja: bombard（砲撃する）+ -ment。ギリシャ語 bombos（ブーンという音）。「砲撃」。bomb と同じ。

en: Nearly; not clearly on one side or the other of a border or boundary, ambiguous.
Of questionable taste or acceptability; approaching bad taste.
Nearly; not entirely but nevertheless to a great extent.
A boundary or accepted division; a border.
A person who has borderline personality disorder.
To border, or border on; to be physically close or conceptually akin to.

ex.en: You really ought to wash your hands of this borderline illegal work.
ex.ja: そろそろこんな犯罪まがいの仕事から足を洗ったらどうなんだ。

en: A single-storey house, typically with rooms all on one level, or sometimes also with upper rooms set into the roof space.
A thatched or tiled one-story house in India surrounded by a wide veranda; a similar house in this style.

bungalow.ety: Borrowed from Gujarati બંગલો (baṅglo, “Bengali-style house; a detached house situated between a garden or a field”). Compare Hindi बंगला (baṅglā, “Bengali”), Bengali বাংলা (baṅla, “Bengal”). Doublet of bangalo and Bangla.

ex.en: Tom and Mary live in a bungalow.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは平屋に住んでいます。

ex.en: The bungalow is approached only by a narrow path.
ex.ja: そのバンガローにいくためには狭い小道しかない。

note.ja: ヒンディー語 baṅglā（ベンガル風の家）から。「平屋」。

en: A person who breaks in to premises with the intent of committing a crime, usually theft.
To commit burglary.

burglar.ety:
16th century, from Medieval Latin burglātor, British byform of burgātor (“burglar”), derived from burgō (“to commit burglary”), from Late Latin burgus (“fortified town”), itself probably from Frankish *burg (“fortress”), from Proto-Germanic *burgz, *burgiją (“borough, watch-tower”).
The -l- in burglātor may have been inserted under influence from Latin latro (“thief”). The shortened English form may have arisen through confluence with Old French burgeor (“burglar”), itself from the same Latin source.

ex.en: The police arrested the burglar on the spot.
ex.ja: 警察は強盗犯を即座に逮捕しました。

ex.en: A burglar broke into the shop last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜、強盗が店に押し入った。

ex.en: A burglar broke in while he was asleep.
ex.ja: 彼が眠っている間に泥棒が入った。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 burglator から。burgus（城砦の町）と関係するとされる。「強盗」。

en: In writing or editing, to write (something: either an entire word or text, or just the initial letter(s) thereof) in capital letters, in …
To contribute or acquire capital (money or other resources) for.

capitalize.ety: From capital + -ize, the first element ultimately from Latin capitālis (“of the head”).

ex.en: The first word of every sentence should be capitalized.
ex.ja: 文の最初の語はすべて大文字ではじめなければならない。

ex.en: I'll help an enemy instead of capitalizing on their distress.
ex.ja: 敵に塩を送る。

ex.en: He capitalized on every opportunity to learn from the great scholar.
ex.ja: 彼はその大学者から学ぶ機会をすべて利用した。

en: A gift or power of leadership or authority.
The capacity to inspire devotion or enthusiasm; personal charm.

charisma.ety:
From Ancient Greek χᾰ́ρῐσμᾰ (khắrĭsmă, “grace, favour, gift”), from χᾰρῐ́ζομαι (khărĭ́zomai, “to show favor”), from χᾰ́ρῐς (khắrĭs, “grace”), from the same root χαρ- (khar-) as χαίρω (khaírō, “to be happy”). Doublet of charism. First attested in 1875.
Outside of theology, as early as 1930, charisma was found in a translation of a book written by German sociologist Max Weber, which OED and Etymonline regards as a semantic loan from German Charisma, denoting the special ability of certain leaders to inspire devotion (sense 1). note.ja: ギリシャ語 kharisma（神の恵み・賜物）から。kharis（恵み）。「カリスマ性」。

A result of a cognitive process.

en: A cookstove.
An appliance or utensil for cooking food.

cooker.ety: From cook + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (patient suffix) (apple; one who is cooked).

ex.en: Do you have a rice cooker at home?
ex.ja: 家に、炊飯器ってある？

ex.en: We cook rice in a rice cooker.
ex.ja: 炊飯器でご飯を炊くよ。

ex.en: I'd like to buy a rice cooker.
ex.ja: 炊飯器が買いたいな。

note.ja: cook（料理する）+ -er。「調理器具」。（英）では「料理人」ではなく「コンロ」。

en: A shallow glass or glass dish, usually with a stem, in which sparkling wine or desserts are served.
An ice cream dessert served in a coupe glass.

coupe.ety: Borrowed from French coupe. Doublet of cup, hive, and keeve.

note.ja: フランス語 coupé（切られた）から。後部を切り詰めた馬車から。coup と同じ。

en: Highly sought-after.
An expression of mild surprise.

ex.en: The fish swam up for crumbs.
ex.ja: パンくずを食べに魚が浮き上がってきた。

en: Shaped like a cylinder.
Describing a map projection in which meridians are mapped onto vertical lines and parallels of latitude onto horizontal lines.

cylindrical.ety: From Latin cylindricus + -al. By surface analysis, cylinder + -ical.

note.ja: cylinder（円筒）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 kylindros（ローラー）、kylindein（転がす）。

en: Likely or attempting to deceive.

deceptive.ety: From Middle French déceptif, from Latin dēceptīvus, from dēcipiō (“to deceive”).

note.ja: de（離れて）+ cept（つかむ）+ ive。人をだます →「人を欺くような・見かけ倒しの」。

en: To hold in belief or estimation; to adjudge as a conclusion; to regard as being; to evaluate according to one's beliefs; to account.
To think, judge, or have or hold as an opinion; to decide or believe on consideration; to suppose.

deem.ety:
From Middle English dēmen (“to judge; to criticize, condemn; to impose a penalty on, sentence; to direct, order; to believe, think, deem”), from Old English dēman (“to decide, decree, deem”), from Proto-West Germanic *dōmijan, from Proto-Germanic *dōmijaną (“to judge, think”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to set, put”).
The word is cognate with Danish and Norwegian Bokmål dømme (“to judge”), Dutch doemen (“to condemn, foredoom”), North Frisian dema (“to judge, recognise”), Norwegian Nynorsk døma (“to judge”), Swedish döma (“to judge, sentence, condemn”), Finnish tuomita (“to judge”). It

ex.en: As long as we cannot deem it safe, we shouldn't take the risk.
ex.ja: 安全だと判断できない以上、危険を冒すべきじゃないんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 dēman（判断する）から。doom（判決）と同じ。「〜と見なす」。

en: The act of devastating, or the state of being devastated; a laying waste.
Waste or misapplication of the assets of a deceased person by an executor or administrator; devastavit.

ex.en: The devastation in Kobe was as terrible as I had imagined.
ex.ja: 神戸の荒廃は、私が想像していたとおり酷いものであった。
